newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Telecom results in line -- analysts.
newsitem.headline: HK Telecom results in line -- analysts.

text.p: Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd's 12 percent earnings growth for the six months to September 30 was generally in line with forecasts, analysts said Tuesday.
"The results were pretty much in line, if just slightly lower, than our forecast," said Philip Wickham, research analyst at G.K. Goh Securities Ltd.
Hongkong Telecom reported net profit of HK$5.39 billion, a 12.1 percent increase over the year-earlier period. Turnover rose to HK$15.92 billion, a 9.3 percent increase,

Analysts said earnings growth was increasingly hamstrung by competition, chiefly from other fixed telephone network service (FTNS) operators offering deeply discounted callback services to compete against Hongkong Telecom in international service.
Internatonal Direct Dial (IDD) accounted for 55 percent of Hongkong Telecom's overall revenues in first half 1996/97.
"Profit margins improved during the period due to cost cutting, but a detailed breakdown is likely to show international call margins falling significantly," said Wickham.

Analysts said they were mildly surprised to see that Hongkong Telecom was able to maintain an average revenue per mobile subscriber of HK$880 per month which was at the high end of the local industry and high by global industry standards.
However, this was certain to come down with growing competition in the mobile phone sector, said one analyst.
Analysts were hesitant to give a revised forecast before reviewing all the factors in this complex industry, but said that there were a few bright spots on the second half horizon.
Looking ahead, China call traffic was likely to be stimulated by a proposed reduction in call rates in China.
For the first half the company reported growth in China call traffic of five percent, compared with non-China growth of 17 percent.

"Growth in China call traffic has been disappointing, but with price decreases forecast for early 1997, together with a pick-up in the Chinese economy, we should see a significant pick up in call traffic and revenues," said Lloyd Fischer, research analyst at BZW Securities Asia.
The China Daily reported on Tuesday that the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications had filed a request to lower international direct dialing rates by the end of 1996 or 1997.
This was forecast to stimulate growth in the volume of calls between Hong Kong and China, which in volume terms is the company's busiest sector.
Wickham said he will be revising down his forecast for the full year but only slightly. His one bright spot in the outlook was the improvement in the defensive nature of the stock.
Previously, Hongkong Telecom traded at a sizeable premium to the market, but the premium has gone with the lower earnings growth rate and the dividend yield looks more attractive.
The share is one of the highest yielding blue chips, he said.
An interim dividend of HK$0.346 was declared. The share closed down HK$0.25 at HK$13.35 on Tuesday.
Hong Kong Telecom is 57 percent owned by Britain's Cable & Wireless.
-- Kathleen Kearney (852) 2843 6933
